question: Herpetologist Deepak Veerappan has a ______ named after him which is known as 'Xylophis deepaki'.
solution:
The correct answer is **__snake__. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Herpetologist Deepak Veerappan has a snake named after him which is known as 'Xylophis deepaki'.**
 
• In the first four months of 2021, the Western Ghats presented new butterflies, frogs, fruit flies, and even freshwater crabs.
 
• Joining the list is a tiny snake of just 20 cm in length with iridescent scales – Xylophis Deepaki. 
 
• It was first stumbled upon on a coconut plantation in Kanyakumari. 
 
• It is now reported to be an endemic species of Tamil Nadu and has been sighted in a few locations in the southern part of the Western Ghats.
 
• The species is named in honour of Indian herpetologist Deepak Veerappan for his contribution to erecting a new subfamily Xylophiinae to accommodate wood snakes.
 
• Wood Snakes:
 
 
• These are harmless (non-venomous), sub-fossorial and often found while digging soil on farms and under the logs in the Western Ghat forests.
 
• They feed on earthworms and possibly other invertebrates.
 
• Their close relatives are found in Northeast India and Southeast Asia and are known to be arboreal (living in trees).
